reader.summary: The week was defined by three intertwined threads: escalating US-Iran and Middle East security, the final stretch of the US midterm campaign, and a renewed push for Ukraine diplomacy. The US ordered the departure of some diplomats and family members from Saudi Arabia and four other Middle East embassies after intelligence warned of Iranian plots to target Americans and Houthi attacks continued, while the USS George Washington repositioned for possible strikes. In the midterm race, Trump ordered the Justice Department to sue to block Alaska's Senate results if the Republican incumbent lost, consumer sentiment slid to near-record lows, and heating oil costs became a flashpoint for Republican candidates. On Ukraine, US envoy Steve Witkoff met Putin in St. Petersburg, Russia freed American prisoner Stephen Hubbard at Trump's request, and Zelensky met US envoys in Oslo ahead of planned three-way talks in Abu Dhabi in early November. Zelensky accused the Pentagon of delaying Patriot missile deliveries. Domestically, the US banned DeepSeek from government systems, the Pentagon announced an 850 F-35 purchase over ten years, and the first Russian diesel tanker under the Trump-Putin deal set sail for American shores.

developments.what_happened: The US ordered some diplomats and families out of Saudi Arabia and four other Middle East embassies as intelligence warned of Iranian plots to kill Americans and Houthi attacks continued, while the USS George Washington repositioned for possible strikes.

developments.subject: US midterm elections
developments.what_happened: Trump ordered the DOJ to sue over Alaska's Senate result, consumer sentiment hit near-record lows, No Kings rallies pushed early voting, and heating oil costs and foreign-policy fallout became flashpoints for Republican candidates.

developments.subject: Ukraine diplomacy and Russia talks
developments.what_happened: Witkoff met Putin in St. Petersburg, Zelensky met US envoys in Oslo, three-way talks were set for Abu Dhabi in early November, and Zelensky accused the Pentagon of delaying Patriot missile deliveries.

developments.subject: Russia releases Stephen Hubbard
developments.what_happened: Russia freed 74-year-old American Stephen Hubbard after more than four years in a Russian jail at Trump's request, and he returned to US soil.

developments.subject: Trade, tariffs, and energy deals
developments.what_happened: The US lifted tariffs on some Canadian goods before the midterms, the first Russian diesel tanker under the Trump-Putin deal set sail, Qatar agreed to buy US LNG through 2054, and Trump was sued over 50 percent tariffs on Canada.

developments.subject: AI and technology policy
developments.what_happened: The US banned DeepSeek from government agency systems, China opposed the ban, DeepSeek raised 15 billion dollars, and SpaceX was reported in talks to acquire cell sites, rattling US telecom stocks.

developments.subject: Alaska Senate lawsuit
developments.what_happened: Trump ordered the Justice Department to file a lawsuit to block certification of Alaska's US Senate results if the Republican incumbent loses, drawing comparisons to past election disputes.

developments.subject: Pentagon F-35 purchase and defense
developments.what_happened: The Pentagon and Lockheed Martin announced a ten-year agreement for 850 F-35 fighter jets, and the Pentagon designated Confucius Institutes a national security threat.

developments.subject: Economic indicators and markets
developments.what_happened: US stocks fell on a deepening tech selloff, initial jobless claims dropped to a three-month low, pending home sales hit a record low, and consumer sentiment approached a record low ahead of the midterms.

developments.subject: Trump's DC arch and golf projects
developments.what_happened: Trump moved forward with his planned 250-foot triumphal arch in Washington despite legal challenges, with construction potentially beginning within two weeks, while a separate golf-course plan for East Potomac Park also drew scrutiny.
